chapter: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
title: Restrictions on mixed bands: the Hollywood Palladium
summary: Barnet says the only restrictions he met were in films and at the Palladium, which would not hire a mixed band.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So the only time you really had -- ran into any absolute restrictions was in films, is that right?
But never any other time. That's great.
No. Except later at the Palladium. Of course we never played there, because they had a -- they wouldn't hire a band that was mixed.
You're talking about the Palladium in Hollywood.
Except they'd hire Harry James because --

Well, Willy was passing and so was Juan, and they didn't show. And of course Joe Comfort played there and he didn't show either, you know. Joe played there with me. That was all right. Which was so ridiculous, you know.
That's really amazing that the Hollywood Palladium is the only -- you never lost any jobs? I mean found out you could not be booked?
